claims.text: Incorporating a controlled volume fraction of WS2 nanoplatelets into the HEA will reduce its coefficient of friction relative to the untreated HEA.
Incorporating a controlled volume fraction of WS2 nanoplatelets into the HEA will reduce its wear rate relative to the untreated HEA.
The reductions in friction and wear will persist across a wide service-temperature range.
Introducing WS2 nanoplatelets during casting or powder metallurgy can produce a uniform dispersion in an in situ HEA composite.
Uniformly dispersed WS2 nanoplatelets will reside at potential sliding interfaces.
WS2 nanoplatelets at sliding interfaces will promote formation of low-shear tribofilms during motion.
WS2 nanoplatelets shear easily at sliding interfaces.
Easy shearing of WS2 nanoplatelets reduces friction.
WS2 nanoplatelets mitigate direct metal-to-metal contact.
Mitigation of direct metal-to-metal contact slows wear.
WS2 nanoplatelets remain an effective self-lubricating phase over a broad temperature range.
The magnitude of friction and wear improvement depends on nanoplatelet content and processing parameters.
The lubrication and wear-reduction effects should persist across the full service-temperature range under the same mechanical loads used for the untreated baseline.
